title: Writing and solving one-step equations
summary: Partners retell short stories as equations of the form x + p = q or px = q, define the variable with units, solve with inverse operations, and check by substituting back into the story.

standard.text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

discourse: Retell a word problem as an equation, explaining what the variable stands for (with its unit) and which quantity in the story is unknown.
Explain solving as undoing the operation in the equation, naming the inverse operation and why it keeps both sides balanced.
Check a solution aloud by substituting it into the equation and into the story: Does 29 stickers plus 12 really make 41?
sentence: Defining the variable: Let s be the number of stickers Jamal had at first.
Equation sentences where is, equals and makes stand for the equal sign: Some number plus 12 equals 41.
Purpose and sequence clauses: I subtracted 12 from both sides to get s by itself; then I checked by ___.
word: Equation versus expression: an equation has an equal sign and makes a claim that can be true or false.
Solve, solution, substitute, inverse operation, both sides.
The multiple-meaning word balance: a balance scale, a bank balance, and keeping your balance.

contentObjective: Students will write and solve equations of the form x + p = q and px = q, including with fractions and decimals, to answer real-world questions.
languageObjective: Students will explain how they wrote and solved an equation using Let ___ be ___, the name of the inverse operation, and a purpose clause (to get ___ by itself).

L1-2: Let x be the number of ___.
x = ___. (Word bank: add, subtract, multiply, divide, both sides)
L3-4: Let ___ be ___. The equation is ___ because ___.
I ___ both sides by ___ to get ___ by itself.
To check, I put ___ back in: ___, so my solution is correct.
L5-6: This story is an addition equation, not a multiplication equation, because ___.
Using the inverse operation keeps the equation balanced, since whatever I do to one side ___.
My solution makes sense in the story because ___; a value like ___ would not, since ___.

vocabulary.definition: a math sentence with an equal sign showing that two amounts are the same
the value of the variable that makes the equation true
vocabulary.morphology: solve + -tion; also means a liquid mixture in science

vocabulary.definition: to put a number in place of a variable
vocabulary.morphology: sub- 'under, in place of' + stitute 'set'; a substitute teacher takes someone's place

vocabulary.definition: an operation that undoes another, such as subtraction undoing addition
the amount you do not know yet; the variable stands for it
vocabulary.morphology: un- 'not' + known; Spanish incógnita has the same idea but a different root

vocabulary.definition: the left and right parts of an equation, on either side of the equal sign
vocabulary.morphology: side means left or right of the equal sign, not a page side

vocabulary.definition: a state where two sides are equal; an equation is like a balanced scale

activity.title: Story to Equation Relay
steps: Each pair gets the four story cards below and a balance-scale mat. Partner A is the Writer and Partner B is the Checker; switch after each card.
The Writer reads the story aloud and says Let ___ be ___ before writing anything. The Checker confirms the unit is included.

The Writer writes the equation and solves it, saying the inverse operation aloud. The Checker substitutes the answer into the equation and into the story and says Correct because ___ or Not yet because ___.
After all four cards, partners sort them into addition equations and multiplication equations and explain one card in each group.
Share: one pair explains the flour card, where the numbers are fractions but the steps are the same.

problems.prompt: Jamal had some stickers. His friend gave him 12 more, and now he has 41. How many stickers did he have at first?
Five notebooks cost $8.75 in all, and each costs the same. What is the price of one notebook?
A recipe needs 2 1/4 cups of flour. Rosa has 3/4 cup. How much more flour does she need?
problems.answer: 1.5 cups, or one and a half cups

problems.prompt: Each lap around the track is 3/4 mile. Lena ran 6 miles. How many laps did she run?

warmup: Show three items: 3x + 5, 3x = 15, and 15 ÷ 3. Partners decide which one is an equation and explain with It is / It is not an equation because ___. Then each partner writes one equation and one expression for the other to sort, and they say the equation aloud using equals or is.
